info.title: Crystalline Fluid API
info.description:
The JSON API `crystalline serve --http` mounts at `/api/v1`, the surface the Fluid UI talks to. Reading is open to any signed-in viewer; writing content needs an editor account and the `If-Match` token of the version being replaced, and account management needs an admin.

Every path but `/auth/login`, `/auth/logout` and `/auth/me` is closed by default: a request that carries no identity is answered 401 ahead of routing, so an unauthenticated caller never learns which paths exist. Every failure is an RFC 9457 problem detail sent as `application/problem+json`.

The payloads marked as generic objects are the engine's own JSON, passed through unchanged so this API and the MCP tools stay one source of truth; each carries an example of the shape it answers with.

get.summary:
`GET /activity` - what was recorded lately, newest first, which is what a
client opens on.
get.description:
The window defaults in the engine rather than here, so the API and the MCP
tool answer the same question when neither is told which window to use.

parameters.name: domains
parameters.description:
Restrict to these domains, comma separated. Defaults to every registered
domain.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: A recency window such as `7d`, `24h` or `2w`. Defaults to `7d`.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Restrict to these `type` values, comma separated.

200.description: The engine's own activity payload, unchanged, with the window it actually used echoed back.

400.description: The query string will not parse.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

post.description: Sets the `fluid_session` cookie and returns the account plus the CSRF token every later mutating request must echo in `x-csrf-token`. Any session the request arrived holding is revoked first, so a planted token cannot survive a login.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set and the CSRF token is in the body.

cache-control.description: `no-store`: this answer carries a session cookie and a CSRF token, so no cache between the server and the browser may keep it.

set-cookie.description: The `fluid_session` session cookie, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.

401.description: The name or password is wrong. One message for every way this can fail, so nothing is learned about which accounts exist.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

422.description: The body is JSON but not a login.

post.summary:
Revoke the session and clear its cookie. Not an error without one: a browser
logging out twice, or with a cookie this server has already forgotten, is
ordinary. Guarded by the CSRF check like any other mutating request, so
another origin cannot log a user out.

200.description: Signed out, whether or not there was a session to revoke.

cache-control.description: `no-store`: this answer clears the session cookie, so no cache between the server and the browser may keep it.

403.description: The identity did not echo its CSRF token, or carries none yet and must call `/auth/me` first, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

get.summary:
The capability probe a client calls before anything else: who it is, whether
it is being served anonymously, whether this instance refuses content
mutations, and which server version it is talking to, so a mismatched UI can
say so instead of failing later.
get.description: Who the caller is, whether it is being served anonymously, whether this instance refuses content mutations, and which server version it is talking to. Also issues the CSRF token every later mutating request must echo in `x-csrf-token`: a cookie session has its token reissued here, and a trusted-header identity is minted a session on the first call, which is the only way that mode obtains a token.

200.description: Who the caller is and what this instance allows. Answered without an identity too, which is how a client learns it has to log in.

cache-control.description: `no-store`. Always set: this answer names the caller and carries their CSRF token, and a shared cache is allowed to store a GET 200 heuristically, which behind an SSO proxy would hand the next user the previous one's identity.

set-cookie.description: The `fluid_session` session cookie, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Set only when this call issues a session, which is the first call from a trusted-header identity whose account holds none; a later probe reuses that session and sets no cookie.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account. The guard resolves identity ahead of routing, so this answer reaches even the paths that are served without one.

get.summary: Upgrade to a real-time co-editing session on one engram.
get.description: WebSocket upgrade for the y-sync + awareness protocol over the engram's shared text. Editor role, a live session cookie and a same-host Origin header are all required and checked before the upgrade; a read-only instance refuses like every write. CSRF headers do not apply to the upgrade GET. Refusals are problem+json.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The domain.

parameters.name: permalink
parameters.description: The engram's permalink; may contain slashes.

101.description: Switching protocols: the session is joined.

403.description: Viewer role, read-only instance, or a missing/foreign Origin.

409.description: Mixed line endings: this file cannot hold a shared session; edit solo.

get.summary:
`GET /context` - the graph around an anchor: the anchored engrams as seed
nodes, the neighborhood ranked out from them, and the edges that connect what
came back. This is what a client draws a relationship view from.
get.description:
The three ways an anchor can be wrong stay distinguishable: absent is a 400
from the extractor, one that is not a `crystalline://` URL is the engine's
own 422, and one pointing at an engram nobody wrote is a 404.

`timeframe` is not exposed: the engine documents it as advisory in this
version, and a parameter that does not change the answer is not worth a
client learning.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: A `crystalline://domain/permalink` anchor. A `/*` suffix globs a prefix.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Traversal depth, 1 to 3. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: domains
parameters.description: Restrict the returned neighborhood to these domains, comma separated.

parameters.name: max_related
parameters.description: Maximum related engrams beyond the anchors. Defaults to 10.

200.description: The engine's own context payload, unchanged: the anchored engrams as seed nodes plus the neighborhood ranked out from them.

400.description: The query string will not parse, `anchor` included: it has no default.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

422.description: The anchor is not a `crystalline://` URL.

get.summary:
`GET /domains` - every registered domain with its counts, its kind and its
routing bullets, plus the behavior rules that govern them.
get.description:
`include_routing` is always on rather than a query parameter: a browser
client is exactly the caller that has no other way to learn what a domain is
for, and the bullets are a handful of lines per domain.

200.description: The engine's own domain listing, unchanged.

behavior: Record what was learned as an engram.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

get.summary: One domain's engrams, filtered by frontmatter and paged.
get.description:
A filter-only search, so the answer carries the same page envelope a search does and a client pages it the same way. Listing by folder is not here: the tree endpoint owns the navigation view and this one owns the frontmatter view.

A domain nobody registered is a 404, while filters that match nothing are an empty page: two states a client can tell apart.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by `type`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by `status`.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description:
Require all of these tags, comma separated. A URL is a string, so the
repeated-parameter form a `Vec` would need is not on offer here; the
list is split on the way in.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only engrams recorded on or after this ISO date.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Defaults to 10.

200.description: The engine's page envelope, unchanged.

hits.snippet: The first engram in this domain.
hits.title: Alpha

400.description: The query string will not parse.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

post.summary: Create an engram from a title and a markdown body.
post.description:
The engine builds the frontmatter and slugifies the title into the filename and permalink, and the account behind the request is named in the engram's `generated.by`.

The answer is the detail read of what landed, `ETag` included, so a client can go straight to editing it. This route never overwrites: a permalink already taken is a 409, and replacing an engram is what the PUT is for.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

201.description: The engine's own read payload for the new engram.

etag.description: The quoted checksum of the engram as written, the token a later save carries in `If-Match`.

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an editor, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

409.description: That permalink is already taken in this domain.

413.description: The body is over the 10 MiB limit this API accepts.

422.description: The body is JSON but not an engram, the title does not slugify to a permalink, the metadata breaks the frontmatter contract, or the target is one of the reserved OKF names (`index.md`, `log.md`).

get.description:
Its frontmatter, its markdown as written and the references the engine resolves around it.

The response carries an `ETag` over the markdown, so a client knows which version it is holding and can say so when it later writes back.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

parameters.name: permalink
parameters.description: The engram permalink. A permalink is a path, so this segment may contain slashes: `notes/deep/gamma`.

200.description: The engine's own read payload, unchanged.

etag.description: The quoted checksum of the engram as read, the same token a later write compares an `expected_checksum` against.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

put.summary: Save an engram's complete markdown text.
put.description:
The text lands verbatim, frontmatter included: nothing rebuilds it and nothing stamps provenance, so a client that saves what it read writes back byte-identical bytes.

The write is guarded by `If-Match`, whose token is the `ETag` of the detail read it is based on: a save that arrives without one is answered 428, and one whose token is stale is answered 412 carrying the version the server holds now, so a client can merge rather than lose the edit.

Editing the `permalink` in the frontmatter moves the engram's address, since the index takes the permalink from the file. Such a save is answered 200 with the engram read at its new address, so a client can follow the move rather than lose track of what it just wrote.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

parameters.name: permalink
parameters.description: The engram permalink. A permalink is a path, so this segment may contain slashes: `notes/deep/gamma`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The quoted `ETag` of the version being replaced, from the detail read.

200.description: The engine's own read payload for the saved engram.

etag.description: The quoted checksum of the engram as saved, the token the next save carries.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or `If-Match` carries more than one entity tag: this surface expects exactly one strong checksum, not a comma-separated list.

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an editor, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account. A read-only instance answers this ahead of the precondition check, so it is never 428.

404.description: No such domain or engram, or the engram is indexed but its file is not on this machine.

412.description: The `If-Match` token is stale. The body carries the version the server holds now, so a client can merge.

413.description: The document is over the 10 MiB limit this API accepts.

422.description: The document is not an engram (unparseable, or no frontmatter block), the `If-Match` is a wildcard or a weak validator, or the target is one of the reserved OKF names (`index.md`, `log.md`).

428.description: No `If-Match` arrived. The token comes from the detail read.

delete.summary: Hard delete an engram, guarded by If-Match.
delete.description: A file domain removes the file from disk; a virtual domain drops the database rows. Guarded the same way `save` is: 428 with no `If-Match`, 412 when the token is stale (carrying the version the server holds now), 204 once it lands. A read-only instance answers 403 ahead of the precondition check, so it is never 428.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

parameters.name: permalink
parameters.description: The engram permalink. A permalink is a path, so this segment may contain slashes: `notes/deep/gamma`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The quoted `ETag` of the version being deleted, from the detail read.

400.description: `If-Match` carries more than one entity tag: this surface expects exactly one strong checksum, not a comma-separated list.

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an editor, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account. A read-only instance answers this ahead of the precondition check, so it is never 428.

412.description: The `If-Match` token is stale. The body carries the version the server holds now, so a client can decide whether losing it is really what it meant.

428.description: No `If-Match` arrived. The token comes from the detail read.

get.summary: The domain's MANIFEST markdown as written.
get.description:
The source, not a reduction of it, so a client can render or edit it directly.

The response carries an `ETag` over the markdown, the same strong validator a later `PUT` compares an `If-Match` against.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

200.description: The manifest source beside the domain it belongs to.

etag.description: The quoted checksum of the manifest as read, the token a later `PUT` carries in `If-Match`.

example.markdown:
---
title: eng
---

## When to Use

- Route here for eng questions.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

404.description: No such domain, or the domain carries no MANIFEST yet.

put.summary: Save a domain's MANIFEST markdown, guarded by If-Match.
put.description: The text lands verbatim, frontmatter included, guarded the same way an engram save is: 428 with no `If-Match`, 412 when the token is stale (carrying the version the server holds now), 200 once it lands. A read-only instance answers 403 ahead of the precondition check, so it is never 428.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The quoted `ETag` of the version being replaced, from the manifest read.

200.description: The manifest as saved, mirroring the GET shape.

etag.description: The quoted checksum of the manifest as saved, the token the next save carries.

---
title: eng
---

## When to Use

- Route here for eng questions.

400.description: `If-Match` carries more than one entity tag: this surface expects exactly one strong checksum, not a comma-separated list.

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an admin, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account. A read-only instance answers this ahead of the precondition check, so it is never 428.

404.description: No such domain, or the domain carries no MANIFEST yet.

412.description: The `If-Match` token is stale. The body carries the version the server holds now, so a client can merge.

413.description: The document is over the 10 MiB limit this API accepts.

422.description: The document carries no frontmatter block, so it is not a MANIFEST.

428.description: No `If-Match` arrived. The token comes from the manifest read.

post.summary: Move an engram to a new path, or into another domain.
post.description:
A same-domain move is a rename; a cross-domain move reads the source content and re-indexes it into the destination's source, rewriting inbound bare links from other domains to the domain-prefixed form.

The permalink rides in the body for the same reason `RetireBody`'s does: the engram route's wildcard cannot be followed by an action segment.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The engram's current domain.

200.description: The move receipt: where the engram came from, where it landed, whether the move crossed domains and how many inbound links were rewritten.

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an editor, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

409.description: The destination already exists in the target domain.

422.description: The destination path is empty, or resolves to one of the reserved OKF names (`index.md`, `log.md`).

post.description:
Sets a retirement `status` (deprecated, superseded or archived), optionally closes out `valid_to`, and for `superseded` wires the reciprocal `superseded_by` / `supersedes` relation pair so verify's T005 and the evolve sweep see a live pair rather than a dangling one.

The permalink rides in the body rather than the path: a permalink is a path of its own and the engram route's wildcard cannot be followed by an action segment.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

200.description: The retirement receipt: domain, permalink, the status now set and the resolved successor permalink, if any.

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an editor, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

404.description: No such domain, engram, or - when status is superseded - successor.

409.description: A conflict the engine's retirement rule raises, answered 409 like the collision this API's other writes raise. Reserved for classification parity with create and move; guided retirement raises no conflict from any input this route accepts today.

422.description: The status is not deprecated, superseded or archived; a successor is missing for superseded or given for another status; the successor resolves to the same engram being retired; or valid_to is not a plain ISO date.

get.summary:
`GET /domains/{domain}/tree` - one domain's engrams and subfolders under a
path, the navigation a file tree in the UI is built from.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The registered domain.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A domain-relative folder path. Defaults to the root.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: How many folder levels deep to list. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: glob
parameters.description: A glob filtering the engram paths listed.

200.description: The engine's own browse payload, unchanged.

400.description: The query string will not parse.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

422.description: The glob is not a valid pattern.

get.summary:
`GET /graph` - the nodes and typed edges around an anchor: every node with
the address, title, status and type a client labels it with, every edge with
its direction and `rel_type`, and `truncated` saying whether the node cap
cut anything.
get.description:
Both bounds are the server's to decide: the engine clamps the depth to one or
two hops and the node count to its own ceiling, so a hand-written URL can ask
neither for nothing nor for a whole index in one payload. A clamped request
is answered rather than refused - the honest report of what was returned is
the payload itself.

Retired engrams are part of the answer, carrying their status. The graph is
the shape of what is written, and a client fades what is retired rather than
being served a graph with the retired nodes already cut out of it.

The three ways an anchor can be wrong stay distinguishable, as on `/context`:
absent is a 400 from the extractor, one that is not a `crystalline://` URL is
the engine's own 422, and one pointing at an engram nobody wrote is a 404.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: A `crystalline://domain/permalink` anchor. A `/*` suffix globs a prefix.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Traversal depth, 1 or 2. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: max_nodes
parameters.description: The most nodes to return. Defaults to 100, capped by the engine.

200.description: The engine's own graph payload, unchanged: the flat node and edge lists a renderer draws from, with `truncated` saying whether the node cap cut anything and `hidden` counting the nodes the cap cut, retired ones first. `id` is opaque and stable only within one response; the address is `crystalline://domain/permalink`.

400.description: The query string will not parse, `anchor` included: it has no default.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

422.description: The anchor is not a `crystalline://` URL.

get.description: Served behind the viewer guard like every other data route: the description of a closed API is part of what being closed by default protects. Tooling does not need this route, since the document is a committed artifact in the repository at `crates/service/openapi/fluid-v1.json`.

200.description: This document. Behind the viewer guard like every other data route.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

get.summary:
`GET /search` - search across the registered domains, or across the ones
`domains` names.
get.description:
The answer is the engine's page envelope (`mode`, `total`, `page`, `limit`,
`count`, `hits`), so a client pages a search the way it pages a listing.
`mode` is the mode that actually ran rather than the one asked for: hybrid
and semantic fall back to text where there is nothing embedded to search, and
the response says which happened rather than quietly answering from a
different index than the caller expected.

A `search_type` the engine does not know is its own error, surfaced as a 422
problem detail carrying the engine's message, so the caller learns which
values do work instead of being handed a bare status.

`metadata_filters` is not exposed: it takes a JSON object of comparisons,
which has no honest query-string spelling, and no client needs it yet.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The free-text query. Omit for a filter-only search.

parameters.name: domains
parameters.description:
Restrict to these domains, comma separated. Defaults to every registered
domain.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by `type`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by `status`.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Require all of these tags, comma separated.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only engrams recorded on or after this ISO date.

parameters.name: search_type
parameters.description: hybrid (default), text, semantic, title or permalink.

parameters.name: min_similarity
parameters.description: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic hit.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Defaults to 10.

200.description: The engine's page envelope, unchanged. `mode` is the mode that actually ran, which may be a fallback to text.

400.description: The query string will not parse.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

422.description: `search_type` names a mode the engine does not know.

get.description: An account carries no password material, so the rows go out as they come back from the store. Admin only: the account list names every way into the instance and who holds it.

200.description: Every account.

403.description: The caller is not an admin, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

post.summary: `POST /users` - add an account, answering 201 with the account as stored.
post.description:
The response is read back out of the store rather than echoed from the
request, so what the client renders is what was written: the folded name,
the defaulted display name, and the disabled flag the row starts with.

403.description: The caller is not an admin, a cookie session did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

422.description: The body is JSON but not an account, or the password is empty.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /users/{name}` - remove an account and every session it holds,
answering 204.
delete.description:
An admin may not remove its own account (409), and the store refuses to
remove the last enabled admin whoever asks (409 as well, in its own words).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The account, in any casing.

204.description: The account and its sessions are gone.

403.description: The caller is not an admin, a cookie session did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

409.description: The account is the caller's own, or is the last enabled admin.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /users/{name}` - change a role, a disabled flag, a display name, or
any combination, answering with the account as it now stands. A password
reset is a separate route, [`reset_password`].
patch.description:
Disabling an account is a revocation as well as an edit: it deletes every
session that account holds, in the store and in the same transaction as the
flag. Setting a role or a display name never touches a session.

Every check runs before the first write, so a request that will be refused
changes nothing. The writes themselves are one store call each rather than
one transaction: the store's guarded statements each own their own
invariant, and a failure part-way leaves the earlier fields applied and says
which operation was refused. That is visible to a client only in the
pathological case of a concurrent edit racing this one, since the refusals a
caller can provoke on purpose - the last-admin guard and an unknown account
- are decided identically by all three statements.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The account, in any casing.

200.description: The account as it now stands.

403.description: The caller is not an admin, a cookie session did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

409.description: The change would disable the caller's own account, or would leave the installation without an enabled admin.

422.description: The body changes nothing: send role, disabled or display.

post.summary:
`POST /users/{name}/password` - replace an account's password, answering
with the account as it now stands.
post.description:
A distinct route rather than a `PATCH` field: setting a password revokes
every session the account holds, in the same transaction as the change -
the reset is useless against a compromised account otherwise, since a
cookie minted before it would keep working for the rest of its life. An
admin resetting their own password signs their own other sessions out too,
this one included.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The account, in any casing.

200.description: The account as it now stands.

403.description: The caller is not an admin, a cookie session did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

post.summary: Pre-save validation: the findings a save would raise, without writing.
post.description:
Runs verify's format (`E`) and temporal (`T`) rule families over the document text, the same families `crystalline verify` runs for a single document. Link, manifest, schema and quality rules need a whole domain for context and are not run here.

`T006` (missing write provenance) is dropped, so a fresh unsaved document is not nagged about a field the save is about to stamp.

Refused like every other write on this surface - editor role, read-only answered first - even though nothing is ever written.

200.description: Every finding, and how many are hard errors.

findings.message: status is `superseded` but no `superseded_by` relation is present

401.description: No identity, or an anonymous one: an identity with no account behind it never writes.

403.description: The caller is not an editor, the request did not echo its CSRF token, this instance is read-only, or the trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

get.summary:
`GET /vocabulary` - the words the domains are written in: the tags in use
with their counts, the observation categories and the relation types, plus
the near-duplicate clusters and tag aliases the engine reports when there are
any.
get.description:
The domain is a filter here rather than a path segment, so an unknown name
answers an empty vocabulary rather than a 404: this route asks what is in
use, and the answer to that can legitimately be nothing.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Restrict to one domain. Omit for a vocabulary across every domain.

200.description: The engine's own vocabulary payload, unchanged. `clusters` and `aliases` are omitted when there are none.

400.description: The query string will not parse.

403.description: The trusted-header identity names a disabled account.

ConflictDetail.description:
The wire form of a 412: a problem detail carrying the version the server
holds now, so a client can show a merge view instead of just failing.

current_content.description: The full markdown the server holds now, so a client can merge.

current_etag.description: The ETag of the version the server holds now, quoted.

CreateBody.description: A new account. `display` defaults to `name` as typed, and `email` is optional and never used for login.

display.description: Human-readable name for the UI. Defaults to `name` as typed.

name.description: The login name, in any casing: the store folds it.

password.description: The initial password. Never stored in the clear; the store hashes it.

role.description: What the new account may do.

CreateEngramBody.description: A new engram. The engine builds the frontmatter from these fields and slugifies the title into the filename and permalink, so the body carries markdown only.

content.description: The markdown body (no frontmatter: creation builds it).

folder.description: A domain-relative subfolder. Defaults to the root.

metadata.description:
Extra frontmatter keys (valid_from, valid_to, salience, ...), passed to
the engine's metadata contract unchanged.

title.description: The engram title. Slugified into the filename and permalink.

type.description:
The engram `type`. Defaults to `engram`. Free form; recommended values
are guidance.

name.description: The account name, in any casing: the store folds it.

LoginResponse.description:
What `POST /auth/login` answers with.

A type rather than an inline `json!`, so the OpenAPI document and the
response are one definition. Same for the two below it.

csrf.description:
The session's CSRF token, which every later mutating request must echo
in the `x-csrf-token` header (see `CSRF_HEADER`).

The header is named in plain backticks rather than through an intra-doc
link because utoipa copies this comment into the published document,
where a Rust link target reads as noise. Same wherever else a schema
field's comment names something in this crate.

user.description: The account that was signed in.

LogoutResponse.description:
What `POST /auth/logout` answers with: an acknowledgement and nothing else,
since a logout that found no session is a success too.

MeResponse.description:
What `GET /auth/me` answers with: everything a client needs before it draws
anything.

anonymous.description: Whether the request is being served as the anonymous viewer.

csrf.description:
The CSRF token of the session this request arrived on, or null when it
arrived on no session.

Reissued here, not only by login, because the session cookie is
`HttpOnly` and the token is not stored anywhere a reload survives: a
browser that refreshes holds a live session whose token it can no longer
produce, and would be unable to log out or to write until it logged in
again. This probe is what a client opens on, so it is where the token
belongs.

Null only for the anonymous viewer, which has no account and can never
write; a trusted-header identity is given a session here on the first
call and handed that same session's token on every later one, so every
identity that can mutate anything carries a token. See the `check_csrf`
rule.

Handing the token back on a `GET` is safe for the same reason handing it
back from login is: no CORS layer exists on this surface, so another
origin can send the request but cannot read the answer. **That is load
bearing - a CORS layer must not be added without revisiting this.**

read_only.description: Whether this instance refuses content mutations.

oneOf.description: The account behind this request, or null when there is none.

version.description: The server version, so a mismatched UI can say so.

MoveBody.description: Move an engram to a new path, or into another registered domain. Inbound bare links are rewritten to the domain-prefixed form on a cross-domain move.

destination.description: The new domain-relative path, with or without `.md`.

destination_domain.description:
Move into another registered domain. Inbound bare links are rewritten
to the domain-prefixed form.

permalink.description: The engram to move, by permalink.

PasswordBody.description: The replacement password. Setting it revokes every session the account holds, this admin's own included when they reset themselves.

password.description:
The replacement password. Setting it revokes every session the account
holds, this admin's own included when they reset themselves.

PatchBody.description: Whichever of the three an admin wants to change. All absent is refused with a 422 rather than served as a no-op, so a client sending the wrong field names hears about it. `display` clears to the login name when sent empty or blank; the password lives on its own route, `POST /users/{name}/password`.

disabled.description:
Whether the account is disabled. Disabling deletes every session the
account holds, so it is a revocation rather than a flag a later
re-enabling hands back; it also stops any new login.

display.description:
The new display name. Empty or blank clears it, resetting the account
to its folded login name - a row is never nameless. Never normalized
like a login name: spaces and casing are kept as sent.

ProblemDetail.description: An RFC 9457 problem detail, sent as `application/problem+json`. Every failure on this surface has this shape, so a client can branch on `status` alone.

detail.description: The specific occurrence, safe to show to the caller.

status.description:
The HTTP status, mirrored into the body so a client that only has the
parsed payload can still branch on it.

title.description: A short, stable, human-readable summary of the problem type.

type.description:
The problem type URI. Always `about:blank`: `status` and `title` carry
the classification, and this surface publishes no per-problem pages to
point at.

RetireBody.description: Guided retirement of one engram: a `status` from a fixed set, an optional close-out date, and, for `superseded`, the successor that wires the reciprocal relation pair.

permalink.description: The engram to retire, by permalink.

status.description: The retirement status: deprecated, superseded or archived.

successor.description:
The successor's permalink, wiring superseded_by / supersedes. Required
for superseded, refused otherwise.

valid_to.description: The date validity ends, plain ISO (YYYY-MM-DD). Absent means unknown.

Role.description:
What a user may do. Ordered least to most privileged; the REST layer maps
each endpoint to the minimum role it accepts.

SaveEngramBody.description: The complete file text, frontmatter included. It is written verbatim: nothing here rebuilds the frontmatter or stamps provenance, so what a client reads back is what its author typed.

content.description: The full markdown text as the editor holds it.
content.example:
---
title: Alpha
permalink: alpha
---

A sharper rule.

SaveManifestBody.description: The full MANIFEST markdown as the editor holds it, written verbatim: nothing here rebuilds the frontmatter or stamps provenance.

markdown.description: The full MANIFEST markdown as the editor holds it.
markdown.example:
---
title: eng
---

## When to Use

- Route here for eng questions.

User.description:
One account. Carries no password material, so it is safe to hand to a
handler and serialize into a response.

disabled.description:
A disabled account keeps its rows but can neither log in nor use an
already-issued session.

email.description: Optional contact address; never used for login.

last_seen.description:
When this account last resolved a session or arrived through the
trusted header, RFC 3339. Null for an account never seen.

name.description:
The login name and primary key. Also the identity the trusted-header
mode provisions against.

UserResponse.description:
What every writing route but `DELETE` answers with: the account as stored,
read back after the write rather than echoed from the request.

user.description: The account as it now stands.

UsersResponse.description:
What `GET /users` answers with. A wrapper rather than a bare array, matching
the `{"users": [...]}` envelope `crystalline users list --json` prints.

ValidateBody.description: The document a save would write, checked without writing. Lives beside the engram routes because what it validates is engram markdown, not because it is scoped to a domain the way the other write routes are.

content.description: The full markdown text, frontmatter included.
content.example:
---
title: Alpha
---

A rule about alpha.

domain.description:
The domain the document belongs (or will belong) to. Names the scan
root in findings; defaults to "draft".

path.description:
The domain-relative path the document sits (or will sit) at. Defaults
to "draft.md".

ValidateFinding.description: One finding, and the envelope: the same fields the verify report carries.

fix.description: A suggested fix, when the rule has one.

line.description: The one-based source line, when the finding points at one.

message.description: What is wrong, in the rule's own words.

rule.description: The rule id, for example E002 or T005.

severity.description: error, warning or info. Hard errors are what a client blocks a save on.

ValidateResponse.description:
What `POST /validate` answers: every finding the format and temporal rule
families raise over the document, and how many of them are hard errors.

errors.description: How many findings are hard errors.

findings.description: Every finding, format and temporal families, default severities.
